title: SIEM export integration workshop — decision log and ops runbook
content:
Purpose:
Notes and decisions from the SIEM export integration workshop (internal working doc). Capture operational runbook items, RBAC v2 mapping choices, audit-event schema proposals, evidence-automation triggers and sample envelopes for Splunk/Datadog/Azure Sentinel. Intended as an interim team artifact to drive engineering and customer onboarding checklists.

Scope:
- Host-side export (Redwood → customer SIEM) for audit and evidence artifacts
- Supported targets: Splunk (HEC), Datadog (Events/Logs API), Azure Sentinel (Log Analytics via Data Collector API / Event Hubs)
- RBAC v2 mapping guidance (service roles → customer SIEM roles)
- Evidence automation hooks (policy → exported artifact) and failure modes
- Minimal connector requirements for production support (throughput, backpressure, redaction)

Attendees:
- Sofia Martinez (owner)
- Daniel Cho (sec eng)
- Aisha Khan (privacy/compliance)
- Liam Patel (platform eng)
- Jordan Rivera (solutions eng)
- plus notes from several customer calls (redacted)

High-level decisions (explicit):
1) Transport modes: we will support both push (HEC / HTTP batch) and pull (SFTP / secure relay) for customers that require egress control. Default is push for hosted customers; dedicated/private can opt to self-host a relay.
2) Envelope canonicalization: every exported record MUST include the same top-level audit fields (timestamp_iso, tenant_id, rbac_principal, action, resource, outcome, request_id, sequence_token). Variants allowed per vendor in an additional vendor_metadata map.
3) RBAC v2 → SIEM role projection: Redwood will emit both the effective RBAC role id and a human-friendly role label. Prototype mapping: role_id (rbacv2:role:xxxx), role_label (e.g., "svc-inference:dedicated-read"). This avoids on-SIEM translation for basic queries.
4) Evidence automation triggers: evidence types (model_inputs, model_outputs, policy_showcase, anomalous_response) are tagged at emit time. Hooks: immediate export for high-priority events (policy_showcase, anomalous_response), batched export for routine audit events (token-usage, route-misses).
5) Redaction policy: by default we redact PII fields (email, ssn, card numbers) in exported payloads. Customers can opt-in to full payload export with a signed Data Access Addendum and KMS integration.
6) Backpressure and retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter up to 15 minutes; after N failures (configurable, default 10) events are queued to dead-letter storage in the customer tenant (if available) and a high-severity alert is emitted to the console.

Audit event canonical schema (required top-level fields) — single-line enforcement list for connectors:
- timestamp_iso (string, RFC3339)
- tenant_id (string)
- environment (string: hosted|dedicated|private)
- rbac_principal (string, rbacv2 principal id)
- role_id (string)
- role_label (string)
- action (string)
- resource_type (string)
- resource_id (string)
- outcome (string: success|failure|throttled|partial)
- request_id (string)
- sequence_token (string, optional for ordered streams)
- severity (string: info|warn|error|critical)
- evidence_type (string: audit|evidence|model-input|model-output|policy)
- vendor_metadata (stringified JSON blob allowed)
- payload_hash (sha256 hex) — recommended for dedupe and integrity checks

Notes on schema: vendor_metadata is intentionally a flexible string field to avoid strict nested objects in early rollouts; connectors should accept it as raw JSON string.

Evidence automation decisioning flow (simplified):
- Event generated → classification (rule engine: static + ML anomaly detector) → classification score + evidence_type assigned → routing policy (immediate export if evidence_type in high_priority_set OR score > threshold) → enrichment (add model version, quantization profile, kernel_profile) → export to target(s) with canonical envelope.

Sample minimal Splunk HEC envelope (text snippet customers/devs can copy):
{
  "time": "2025-02-14T16:03:12Z",
  "host": "redwood-inference",
  "source": "redwood.audit.events",
  "sourcetype": "redwood:siem:audit",
  "event": {
    "timestamp_iso": "2025-02-14T16:03:12Z",
    "tenant_id": "org_12345",
    "environment": "hosted",
    "rbac_principal": "user:alice",
    "role_id": "rbacv2:role:reader",
    "role_label": "platform-reader",
    "action": "model.generate",
    "resource_type": "model_endpoint",
    "resource_id": "endpoint-prod-1",
    "outcome": "success",
    "request_id": "req_987654321",
    "sequence_token": "seq-0001",
    "severity": "info",
    "evidence_type": "model-output",
    "vendor_metadata": "{\"model_version\":\"redwood-v1.3\",\"quant\":\"int8\"}",
    "payload_hash": "2b7e151628aed2a6abf7158809cf4f3c"
  }
}

Sample Datadog log envelope (HTTP):
{
  "ddsource": "redwood",
  "service": "inference-api",
  "host": "redwood-inference",
  "message": "redwood audit event",
  "timestamp": 1707933792,
  "attributes": {
    "tenant_id": "org_12345",
    "rbac_principal": "user:alice",
    "action": "model.generate",
    "outcome": "success"
  },
  "vendor_metadata": "{\"model_version\":\"redwood-v1.3\"}"
}

Sample Azure Sentinel (Log Analytics) record (fluent-style):
{
  "TimeGenerated": "2025-02-14T16:03:12Z",
  "TenantId": "org_12345",
  "ResourceType": "model_endpoint",
  "ResourceId": "endpoint-prod-1",
  "Principal": "user:alice",
  "Action": "model.generate",
  "Outcome": "success",
  "EvidenceType": "model-output",
  "VendorMetadata": "{\"kernel_profile\":\"ampere_xm_1\"}",
  "RequestId": "req_987654321"
}

Connector capability checklist (must-have for GA):
- Authentication: HEC token / Datadog API key / Azure Managed Identity or shared key for Log Analytics
- TLS 1.2+ with strong ciphers; client cert option for private relays
- Delivery guarantees: at-least-once with configurable dedupe window and payload_hash support
- Backpressure handling & local bounded queue (configurable size)
- Redaction hooks (pre-export pipeline stage) with a plugin for regex/PII detectors
- Configurable batching window (ms) and max batch size (events)
- Metrics & tracing: per-tenant export success/failure, queue depth, avg latency (exposed to Console)
- Dead-letter storage and retrieval API with retention policy mapped to customer SLA

Operational runbook (short):
- On connector failure alerts: page on-call SRE, flip connector to fail-open or fail-closed based on customer SLA (policy stored in tenant metadata)
- If export backlog > 10k events for > 30m: escalate to platform infra; enable temporary burst throttling on upstream models to protect runtime resources
- If repeated 401/403 to target: check keys/certs, check tenant opt-in (DPA / Data Addendum signed). Rotate keys and notify customer.
- If PII-redaction error reported: mark incident, pause exports for affected tenant, run targeted revalidation, allow opt-in full export only after DPA and KMS test.

Open questions / risks (to track):
- Legal: acceptable minimal retention for evidence artifacts in dead-letter — coordinate with legal for region-locked retention policies.
- Performance: how does vendor_metadata as string affect downstream indexing costs in large Splunk estates? Need sample cost modeling.
- Ordering: sequence_token semantics for multi-shard connectors (Sentinel via Event Hubs) require per-tenant shard affinity — design follow-up.
- Compliance: export of model inputs may be restricted in certain regulated verticals — need a gated opt-in flow in Console.

Action items (owner — due):
- Liam: prototype vendor_metadata as string vs nested object benchmark for Splunk and Datadog indexing (2025-02-28)
- Daniel: draft RBAC projection mapping table and sample queries for SOC teams (2025-03-05)
- Aisha: produce DPA addendum template for evidence export opt-in (2025-03-10)
- Sofia: update Console export UI to show status and dead-letter counts per tenant (2025-03-12)
- Jordan: create customer-facing one-pager describing redaction defaults and opt-in flow (2025-03-07)

Notes to reviewers: this doc is a working artifact; please add inline comments or push changes to the Confluence draft. Once engineering accepts the connector checklist and the initial prototype passes a customer pilot (>= 2 customers across Splunk/Datadog/Sentinel), we will promote to the official runbook and publish a versioned spec.

Appendix A — quick glossary (for SOC & customer teams):
- evidence_type: logical tag used by Redwood to classify exported artifacts
- vendor_metadata: opaque enrichment blob that adapters may parse into vendor fields for indexing
- sequence_token: optional field used when ordering matters (per-tenant incremental counter)
- dead-letter: tenant-scoped storage for failed exports awaiting replay

End of document.
